description: Crop-specific canopy heat thresholds (deg F), risk formula weights, and Q10 spoilage parameters for PeachState CoolChain demo (Georgia, USA). Risk = 100 * clamp(sum(w_i * z_i)) where z are standardized proxies (canopy temp relative to threshold, exceedance hours, persistence).

peach.name: Peach
peach.notes: Demo hero crop. 95F = brown rot acceleration, 100F = critical softening. Alert crop: PV-07.
sources: UGA Extension Circular 1173 - Peach Growing Degree Days / heat-unit thresholds
UGA College of Ag - Peach production & postharvest heat guidance

pecan.name: Pecan
pecan.notes: Nut fill stage: 95F = poor kernel quality, 100F = shuck decline. GDD base 55F per UGA pecan heat-unit guidance (Southeastern Pecan Growers Handbook, UGA C-1174 Pecan Management Calendar).
sources: UGA Pecan Extension - 'Pecans and Heat' (Lenny Wells, site.extension.uga.edu/pecan/2022/06/pecans-and-heat/)
Southeastern Pecan Growers Handbook (UGA/Auburn/USDA), heat-unit base 55F

blueberry.name: Blueberry
blueberry.notes: 90F = accelerated decay, 95F = anthocyanin loss. Most sensitive of the four.
sources: UGA Extension - Blueberry production (Southeast Regional Blueberry Handbook)
USDA ARS blueberry postharvest heat-stress guidance

vidalia_onion.name: Vidalia onion
vidalia_onion.notes: 85F = sprouting risk in curing/transit, 90F = rot. Curing sheds are heat-sensitive stage.
sources: UGA Extension - Vidalia onion curing & storage (Vidalia Onion & Vegetable Research Center)
UGA B 1327 - Sweet Onion Storage / heat-sprout thresholds

community.name: Community / residential
community.notes: Mixed vegetables / greens. Used for Scene 5 community gardens + last-mile delivery.
sources: UGA Extension - Home/community garden heat management (general)
USDA H66 - The Commercial Storage of Fruits, Vegetables, and Florist and Nursery Stocks (Q10 spoilage rates)

q10_reference: USDA Agriculture Handbook No. 66 'The Commercial Storage of Fruits, Vegetables, and Florist and Nursery Stocks' (Q10 spoilage acceleration per 10C rise)
gdd_method: GDD = max(0, ((Tmax + Tmin)/2) - base); bases: peach/blueberry/community 50F, pecan 55F, Vidalia onion 40F. UGA CAES Circular 1320 documents the standard GDD calculation (base + optional 86F cap for warm-season crops).
sources_overall: UGA Cooperative Extension (extension.uga.edu) - pecan, peach, blueberry, onion production guidance
UGA CAES Field Report C-1320 'Growing Degree Days for Sweet Corn in Southern Georgia' (GDD method)
USDA Agriculture Handbook No. 66 (Q10 / storage spoilage)
Andersen & Brodbeck 1988, J. Amer. Soc. Hort. Sci. 113:444-450 (pecan heat tolerance: photosynthesis to 106F leaf temp with adequate water)
